title: Meet Your New Helper Robot
text:
Congratulations on your new Helper Robot 3000! Please read these instructions before you turn it on.

To start your robot, pull the {adjective} lever on its back and say its name {adverb}. It will open its eyes, beep twice, and ask for a {noun}. This is normal. Your robot can sweep the floor, fold the laundry, and {verb} while you sleep.

Every night, plug your robot into the wall and give it a snack of {number} {plural noun}. Do not let it near water or {plural noun}. If your robot starts {verb ending in ing} in the kitchen, it is just happy.

If you have a problem, check the little screen on its chest. A {color} light means it needs a nap. A blinking light means it {past tense verb} into the closet again. A funny smell means it ate your {plural noun}. For help, please call our {adjective} helper line and ask for {name}.

title: Diary of a Robot Who Loves to Dance
text:
Dear Diary,
My name is Unit Six. I work at the cookie factory, where I put {plural noun} on cookies all day. It is a {adjective} job, but secretly I want to be a dancer.

Today after work, I practiced in the parking lot. First I spun around {number} times. Then I tried to {verb} like the people on TV. My arms went one way, my wheels went the other way, and I {past tense verb} right into a {noun}.

A little girl named Rosa saw me. She did not laugh. She showed me a dance called the {silly word}. You wiggle your {body part}, clap your hands {adverb}, and spin like a {adjective} washing machine.

Tomorrow I will teach the dance to the other robots. We will practice every day at lunch, right next to the {plural noun}. My boss will be so {adjective} that she will start {verb ending in ing}.

title: Rules for the Robot Science Fair
text:
Welcome to the Maple Street Robot Science Fair! Every robot must follow these rules.

All robots must be shorter than the gym door and lighter than a {noun}. Each robot must do one helpful job, like sweeping, sorting socks, or carrying {number} {plural noun} at once. Robots may not {verb} during the judging. Last year a robot did that, and the judges {past tense verb} for a week.

Please keep your robot's battery charged. If your robot runs out of power, it might start {verb ending in ing} in the corner. Please do not feed your robot {plural noun}. It is bad for the wires. Robots must also keep their {body part} off the snack table.

First prize is a shiny trophy and a {adjective} ribbon. Second prize is a {noun}. Mr. Ortiz, our {adjective} judge, will walk {adverb} past each table and take notes. Good luck, and may the best robot {verb}!

title: Wanted: A Robot to Walk the Dog
text:
Wanted: one friendly robot to walk our dog, Noodle. Noodle is small, fluffy, and very {adjective}. He weighs about as much as a {noun}.

Noodle needs a walk every morning at seven. He likes to stop and sniff every tree, mailbox, and {noun} on our street. The robot must hold the leash {adverb} and never let Noodle {verb} in the mud. Noodle does not like {plural noun}, so please walk around them.

After the walk, the robot will give Noodle a {adjective} bath and a treat shaped like a {food}. Noodle also likes to hear songs about {plural noun}. Our last robot sang to him every day, but it {past tense verb} so loudly that the neighbors closed their windows.

The pay is {number} shiny bolts a week and all the oil you want. If you are good at {verb ending in ing}, please knock on the {color} door at our house.

title: Robot Wins the Town Pie Contest
text:
This just in from the Pine Hill Fair! For the first time ever, a robot has won the town pie contest. The robot, named Gizmo, baked a {adjective} pie filled with apples and {plural noun}.

The judges took one bite and {past tense verb} right out of their chairs. "It tastes like {food} and sunshine," said Judge Patel. "I have never had anything so {adjective}." Gizmo says the secret is to stir the filling {adverb} and to {verb} while the pie bakes. Gizmo also adds a pinch of {plural noun}.

Last year's winner, Mrs. Green, was a good sport. She shook Gizmo's metal {body part} and asked for the recipe. Gizmo printed it out on a long strip of paper.

Gizmo won a blue ribbon, a brand-new {noun}, and a year of free {plural noun}. Next year, Gizmo plans to bake {number} pies and spend the summer {verb ending in ing} at the beach.

title: Robo-Chef's Famous Tuesday Soup
text:
Hello, I am Robo-Chef, and this is my famous Tuesday soup. It is the favorite soup of everyone at the robot repair shop.

First, fill a big pot with water and three {plural noun}. Turn on the stove and wait until the water is {adjective}. Next, chop one carrot, two potatoes, and a {noun}. Drop them in {adverb}, one at a time.

Now it is time for my secret ingredient: a pinch of {plural noun}. Stir the soup with your longest {body part} for {number} minutes. If the soup starts to {verb}, that means it is almost ready. If it smells {adjective}, add more salt.

Pour the soup into a {adjective} bowl and top it with a little {food}. My helpers like to eat it while {verb ending in ing} by the window. Enjoy, and do not forget to {verb} your bowl when you are done!

title: A Thank-You Note to My Robot Vacuum
text:
Dear Beep-Bop,
Thank you for cleaning our house every single day. You are the most {adjective} vacuum in the whole neighborhood. You zoom {adverb} under the couch and come out covered in {plural noun}.

I am sorry about last Tuesday. I did not mean to leave a {noun} in the hallway. It got stuck in your wheels, and you {past tense verb} in a circle for an hour. Grandma says you sounded like "{sound}" the whole time.

Also, thank you for not eating my {plural noun} this week. I know you wanted to. Mom says I must pick up my toys and never {verb} near your brushes. Dad says you can {verb} in the garage on Saturdays.

To say thank you, I made you a {adjective} sticker shaped like a {food}. I hope you like it. Please keep {verb ending in ing} and being our {adjective} friend.
Love,
Penny

title: A Chat with the Robot Crossing Guard
text:
Our school paper talked to Bolt, the robot crossing guard on Elm Street. Bolt is tall, shiny, and a little bit {adjective}. Bolt has worked there for {number} years and never missed a day.

First, we asked about the best part of the job. "I love to {verb} with the kids every morning," Bolt said. "And I get to hold a {adjective} stop sign." Next, we asked what Bolt eats for lunch. "Mostly oil with a sprinkle of {food}," said Bolt. "But on Fridays I have a plate of {plural noun} and a {adjective} cookie."

Then we asked about Bolt's busiest day. Bolt said a {noun} rolled into the street, and a duck family {past tense verb} right behind it. "I stopped all the cars," Bolt said {adverb}. "Then I helped the ducks carry their {plural noun}."

Last, we asked for advice. "Always look both ways and hold a grown-up's hand," said Bolt. "Once you are on the sidewalk, you may {verb} like a {animal} all the way to class. Wear something {color} so drivers see you."

title: Robot Day at Oak Hill School
text:
Good morning, Oak Hill School! This is Principal Brooks with a special announcement. This Friday is Robot Day!

Every student is invited to dress up as a robot. You can use boxes, tin foil, and as many {plural noun} as you want. Please do not wear anything bigger than a {noun}, or you will not fit through the door.

In the morning, the music teacher will teach everyone a {adjective} robot dance. You will move your arms {adverb}, wiggle your {body part}, and say "{silly word}" every time you turn. At lunch, the cafeteria will serve robot pizza topped with little bolts made of {food}.

In the afternoon, we will have a parade around the playground. The best costume wins a {adjective} trophy and the chance to {verb} with me on the morning announcements. Remember, robots never {verb} in the halls. Robots walk {adverb}, and they love {verb ending in ing}. Beep boop, and have a {adjective} day!

title: Robot School Report Card
text:
